title: Company Profile Lookup Output
description: Output of the company-profile-lookup Brick. All eight fields are always present on Success. Facts resolved from the catalog are nonempty strings when profile_found is true; null when profile_found is false. The if/then/else block below enforces this cross-field invariant at the schema layer; the Brick implementation enforces it at runtime.

company_url_normalized.description: Normalized hostname: lowercased ASCII, with any leading 'www.' and single trailing dot stripped, scheme and path removed. 253 is the DNS hostname length cap; the Brick additionally validates DNS-label syntax.

profile_found.description: True iff the normalized hostname matched a catalog entry. See the if/then/else block below: true requires the four fact fields to be nonempty strings; false requires all four to be null.

company_name.description: Fictional display name from the catalog. Null when profile_found is false. For v0.1 the catalog contains three fictional profiles under IETF-reserved example.com subdomains; this is not a real-company fact.

industry.description: Canonical industry label from the catalog. Null when profile_found is false.

segment.description: Canonical market-segment label from the catalog. Null when profile_found is false.

audience.description: Canonical audience label from the catalog. Null when profile_found is false.

target_icp.description: Passthrough of input.target_icp, unchanged. Carried through this Brick so the downstream qualifier can interpret it after edge mapping.

notes.description: Passthrough of input.notes, unchanged. When input.notes was absent or null, this is null -- always present in output so the edge mapping never encounters a missing source path.
